note: Version-controlled resource policy. 'current' fields are read from deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.yml by tools/resource-limits/check.mjs on every run. 'measured' is null everywhere: no baseline has been taken, so no expected-peak or headroom number is claimed. Thresholds are starting targets from the standard, for owner review.

hostinger.note: Shared Dokploy host. Size not recorded anywhere in the repo; ask the operator (RES-002). Setting memoryBytes turns the host-budget check from BLOCKED into a real comparison.

prod-reference.note: docker-compose.prod.yml is the reference single-VM topology (assumes 16 GB+ per its own comment); it is not what runs at desk.wabo.ai.

acceptedGaps.reason: No container has a CPU limit on a host shared with other apps. Needs the host's core count and a measured baseline before choosing numbers; the proposed values are in the deployment-limits patch for owner review.
No container has a PID limit. Same patch.
Host RAM is not recorded. Steady-state limits sum to 4.44 GiB and the blue-green release overlap to 6.19 GiB; whether that fits is unknown until the operator fills hosts.hostinger.memoryBytes.
Summed worker concurrency is 171 against a pool of 10. Most jobs wait on providers, not the database, so this is a risk to measure, not a proven fault; needs pool wait metrics (RL-08) first.

maxmemory 192mb in a 256m container is 75%. An AOF rewrite forks, and a queue Redis that keeps writing during the rewrite can need close to double the data size; the kernel then kills Redis and in-flight queue state since the last fsync is lost. The deployment-limits patch sets the container to 320m (60%) for owner review.
docker-compose.prod.yml is the reference topology and is not deployed; it sets no limits.
Same as above; also a Redis with no maxmemory grows until the container or host is out of memory.
